messages:
Nora: Little PSA from today  router was behind my monstera and apparently the plant loves the warmth. Leaves tangled in antenna, performance mystery solved. photo: https://i.imgur.com/monstera-router.jpg :seedling:
Felix: legendary. Plant wins again. Did you notice packet loss or just slow browsing?
Nora: Mostly intermittent Zoom glitches and pages that would hang, weird enough that I rebooted twice before I glanced behind the plant.
Emi: tip: routers + plants = humidity party. Might accelerate corrosion. Mount the router a bit higher if you can.
Harpreet: Also, pro-solution: cheap rack shelf or adhesive wall mount. Keeps cats, plants, and coffee away.
Nora: Ordered a clip mount. Also re: desk aesthetic debate  should all routers be hidden for beauty or visible for signal? Vote: hidden vs visible?
Felix: Visible for signal. Hidden for looks. Prioritize stability.
Emi: Visible. Also side poll: who uses a mesh vs single big router?
Harpreet: Mesh here. Apartment has weird concrete walls.
WiFiBot: ISP note: Nora's subnet experienced 2 minutes of packet loss at 10:38. Signal restored after repositioning.
Emi: Quick checklist for anyone with spotty WFH wifi: 1) elevation, 2) distance from microwave/kettle, 3) avoid metal cabinets, 4) enable 5GHz for short-range devices.
Felix: Adding: keep a cheap travel router in the WFH drawer for emergencies. Mine saved me during a week-long outage.
Nora: Thanks all. Learned two things: move router off the floor and stop naming plants router-adjacent things. My monstera will now be called "Signal Thief." :laughing:
